mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points within a three-month window signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in real personal consumption (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate weakening demand that triggers corporate revenue concerns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High labor market tightness (UNRATE below 4.0% and PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly) accelerates wage inflation, prompting Fed tightening that depresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the labor market tightness condition, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1.0% signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicate monetary tightening that raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint increase in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Early-cycle expansion (RSAFS growth above 0.5% monthly) supports consumer spending momentum that drives corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting the early-cycle expansion condition, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
